item: implement the freshness-receipts gate owed by MASTER_MICKEY17_V2_20260924.md row 8 (lane agentcheck): small tool tools/freshness_gate.py that takes a receipt markdown path and verifies it carries a fetch/source freshness stamp (dated line like source-fetched: YYYY-MM-DD), exit 0 if present + parseable date within N days (arg --days, default 14), exit 2 otherwise; tests for fresh passes / stale fails / missing stamp fails; run pytest + ratchet --changed and cite raw output
note: tools/freshness_gate.py landed, standalone (t11a's tools/quote_gate.py verified absent on disk, so style taken from tools/freshness_check.py and tools/workflow_gate.py: --self-test, exit 2 is the only hard block). Accepted labels: source-fetched / source_fetched / source fetched / fetched / observed-at / observed_at, case-insensitive, optional ISO time suffix; most recent stamp in the file is the evidence. Fail-closed: missing stamp, unparseable calendar date, stale, future-dated beyond 1d skew tolerance (fabrication smell), and missing file are all exit 2 with a stated reason, never a traceback. Contract proven live: fresh_exit=0, stale_exit=2, none_exit=2, --days 30 flips stale to 0, absent_exit=2. Negatives recorded: my own first draft carried a real em-dash in the tool docstring header, caught by the gate's own law test plus manual scan, fixed before banking; full-scope ratchet (without --changed) currently fails on 9 pre-existing NEW hits in files this gopher never touched, recorded not repaired; estate-wide 1341-test suite not run this item, scope was the two new files plus the changed-scope gate.

next_steal: the gate reads one stamp line but does not bind the stamp to a source hash, so a receipt can re-stamp old claims with a fresh date; next steal is receipt(observed_at, source_hash) pairing per MASTER row 8: require the stamp line to sit next to a source-hash line and have the gate verify the hash against the cited artifact when the file is local, making re-stamping detectable
